I have grown sorghum on this same land since I was a boy, and everything I know I learned from my father and from watching my neighbors here in Nsanje. I will spread manure from my goats on the plot because that costs no money and it is what my father always did, and I will plant the seed I kept from last year’s harvest — sorghum is a strong crop that does not need those expensive chemical bags. My wife and grandchildren will work this plot with me, about fifty-five days from the first hoeing to the threshing, because we cannot pay hired workers when cash is so tight.
